title: Connecticut National Guard Crew Goes on Rescue Missions, Sept. 21, 2018 (Prime Cuts/Interviews)
description:
LOCATION: RALEIGH, N.C.
DESCRIPTION: Connecticut National Guardsmen board a
UH-60 Blackhawk helicopter to preform search and rescue
missions in North Carolina during the response to 
Hurricane Florence, Sept. 21, 2018.

INTERVIEW @ 01;25
NAME: Sgt. Michael Justo 
TITLE: Army National Guard Crew Chief, Company C, 
3rd Battalion, 142 Aviation Regiment

INTERVIEW @ 04;30
NAME: CW2 Robert Borden
TITLE: Army National Guard Pilot, Company C, 3rd Battalion, 
142 Aviation Regiment 

INTERVIEW @ 06;48
NAME: Sgt. Ryan Gummoe
TITLE: Army National Guard Crew Chief, Company C, 
3rd Battalion, 142 Aviation Regiment

transcript.text: Michael, Justo, Charlie Company, third of the 142nd Air Salt.
Trying to throw it.
What is your position?
I am a crew chief.
And as well as a crew chief, I am a crew chief flight instructor.
What does a crew chief do?
We're responsible for all the maintenance of the aircraft, making sure the aircraft is all set for the pilots.
They get the easy job, they just come out and fly it.
We pretty much prepare everything for the documentation as well as scheduling the maintenance, performing the maintenance, and making sure the aircraft is all set.
We also do the inflight duties of airspace clearing and then, during events like this, operating rescue voice and calling the aircraft clear, not clear, whatever it needs to do.
So tell me a little bit about your mission down here.
We were initially given a task about 18 hours from when we left of, hey, go down there and bring whatever you need to support them.
So we kind of took a guess, thinking we might need our rescue voice as far as, or doing medevac transportation.
That's what we brought our medevac with us and general support, having seats or removing the seats for cargo.
So pretty much we came down here with the, any adventure we might need to do.
Okay, so I heard you guys had to do a hoist rescue.
What was that like?
Which one?
The one with the lady and her dog.
The one with the lady and her dog.
That was actually, we were done doing an initial search pattern.
We saw quite a few people that decided they didn't need to be rescued.
They were going to try and stick it out.
They had boats or they were fine on top of their house.
We were going back for fuel.
I was on the right side of the aircraft and I saw a lady waving a sheet.
So put it in a bank, noticed that she had three people with her that were signaling for rescue.
So we were working with the Oklahoma National Guard on each heart teams, the helicopter searching rescue teams.
Hooked him up to the hoist, put him down and ended up rescuing one woman.
She came up and unfortunately half way up, our hoist had an internal failure.
So we're trained, we do hoist operations, generally trying to do it as much as we can.
We trained for that adventure already so we just moved the aircraft over, put her down, put the aircraft down,
and we're able to load her up into the aircraft.
Okay.
So what's coming about your mission overall with helping out your fellow countrymen here with it when they're in their time of need?
Overall we started off with the heart team or the HSTART teams, the helicopter search and rescue teams.
We did that for a few days and then by the end of it I wasn't able to fix the hoist and everything.
So we switched over to SNS missions, service and supply missions.
So far as moving passenger, moving people, cargo, we did a mission, we removed 13,000 pounds of food in four trips to Wilmington Hospital.
Because they were completely, the town itself was completely cut off by roads.
And then as you guys saw we did a passenger transportation, then we did that yesterday, a lot of passenger movement.
Just bringing people to where they need to be. Some places that are not accessible by vehicle.
How do you feel about being called up to go help out your fellow countrymen in their time of need?
Feels good. You know, we get back to the National Guard mission. Some of us just got back from deployment and everything.
You know, we've been focused on doing the overseas deployment. Everything feels good to get back to the state missions and everything.
And we're all part of the same country so we're going to help our states as much as we can.
Okay, let's go ahead and tell me your first and last name, Rank and Position.
Chief Foreign Officer 2 Rob Borden, my instructor pilot with Charlie Company 3142.
Okay, so tell me about your little bit about your mission down here sir.
We originally were activated last Wednesday for a come down here, help out with hurricane relief.
We staged out of Knoxville, Tennessee and then on Saturday we transitioned over here to start assisting with the hurricane relief.
Okay, so I heard you guys had a hoist rescue mission. Tell me a little bit about that?
We actually, the second day we were down here we were able to get two hoist missions completed.
We found a family that was stranded at their house up on their deck. Thankfully they were able to get down to their yard.
We had a little bit more room and we were able to lower our rescue swimmers down to them.
He secured one of the young ladies and her dog and we were able to get them back up to the aircraft and get them over the hospital at Wilmington.
Okay sir, so tell me how does it make you feel coming out here and helping fellow countrymen in their time of need?
We're just doing our job out here. This is what we trained for.
I've been doing the flight school or the flight thing since 2013 and we thoroughly enjoy getting these things and being able to help out our fellow countrymen and be able to get those
rescue missions completed and get people the safety so that they're not stranded in their houses flooded with water.
Tell me a little bit about the supply mission to the Wilmington Hospital.
That was actually a pretty interesting mission. We had a mission request for transporting 14,000 pounds of food from the airport all the way over to Wilmington Hospital.

We were transporting and took us four halls fully loaded the back of the black hawk with everything from frozen chicken and bacon to coffee creamer to just basic knees, bread, milk, whatever they needed.
Alright, anything else you'd like to answer?
No, good.
Hunter Crudu.
Crudu did phenomenal.

These guys in the back, our maintainers and our medics have been really working hard myself and the other pilot have been just kind of sitting up front wiggling sticks and these guys have been really doing a bolt of the work.
Okay, go ahead and tell me your first and last name, Rankin Unit.
It's Brian Gummo, Sergeant, Charlie Compe, and third of the one, four, two.
Okay, so tell me a little bit about your mission down here.
The first day we were doing a search and rescue and then since that day we've been just out doing admin transporting supplies people.
Okay, so I heard you had a hoist rescue with a woman or a dog. Can you tell me a little bit about that?
Yeah, we were actually on our way back to go get fuel and as we flew over they pulled out a white sheet and flagged us down.
So we turned around and we sent our swimmer down and she hooked her up in front of her porch and pulled her up to the aircraft.
So how do you feel about helping out your fellow countrymen in their time of need?
Oh, it feels great. Just doing my job right now.
